Traditional Scottish Venison Pies

Served at: St. Andrew's Day

Serves 4-6Prep 30 minCook 2 hours 30 min

These hearty venison pies are a perfect centerpiece for a St. Andrew's Day celebration, Scotland's national day on November 30th. Rich, savory, and warming, they embody the spirit of Scottish comfort food, ideal for a late autumn gathering with friends and family. The tender venison slow-cooked in a flavorful gravy, encased in a golden pastry, offers a taste of the Scottish Highlands.

Ingredients

  • 2 tablespoons (30ml) olive oil or butter
  • 1.5 pounds (680g) venison stewing meat, cut into 1-inch (2.5cm) cubes
  • 1 large onion, chopped
  • 2 carrots, peeled and diced
  • 2 celery stalks, diced
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 cup (120ml) dry red wine (like Cabernet Sauvignon or Merlot)
  • 2 cups (480ml) beef or venison broth
  • 1 teaspoon dried thyme
  • 1 bay leaf
  • 1 teaspoon salt, or to taste
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, or to taste
  • 1 sheet (about 14 ounces/400g) ready-made shortcrust pastry, chilled
  • 1 sheet (about 14 ounces/400g) ready-made puff pastry, chilled
  • 1 large egg, beaten (for egg wash)

Method

  1. Heat olive oil or butter in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
  2. Pat the venison cubes dry with paper towels and season generously with salt and pepper.
  3. Brown the venison in batches, ensuring not to overcrowd the pot, until seared on all sides. Remove the browned venison with a slotted spoon and set aside.
  4. Add the chopped onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté over medium heat for 8-10 minutes, until softened, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
  5. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
  6. Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir well, cooking for 1-2 minutes to cook out the raw flour taste.
  7. Pour in the red wine, scraping the bottom of the pot to deglaze and release any stuck-on bits. Bring to a simmer and cook for 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced.
  8. Return the browned venison to the pot. Add the beef or venison broth, dried thyme, and bay leaf. Stir well.
  9. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and cook for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until the venison is very tender. Stir occasionally.
  10. Remove the bay leaf and check seasoning, adding more salt and pepper if needed. Let the filling cool completely before assembling the pies; this prevents soggy pastry.
  11. Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C). Lightly grease 4-6 individual pie dishes or a single 9-inch (23cm) pie dish.
  12. On a lightly floured surface, roll out the shortcrust pastry and use it to line the bottom and sides of your pie dishes. Trim any excess pastry.
  13. Spoon the cooled venison filling into the pastry-lined dishes, filling them generously.
  14. Roll out the puff pastry and cut out lids to fit your pie dishes. Place the puff pastry lids over the filling, pressing the edges firmly to seal them to the shortcrust base.
  15. Cut a small slit or make a few holes in the center of each pie lid to allow steam to escape during baking.
  16. Brush the tops of the pies with the beaten egg wash for a golden finish.
  17. Place the pies on a baking sheet and bake for 30-40 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown and puffed, and the filling is bubbling. If the tops brown too quickly, you can loosely tent them with aluminum foil.
  18. Let the pies rest for 5-10 minutes before serving. Serve hot.

Tips

  • For an extra layer of flavor, add 1 cup (100g) of sliced mushrooms to the pot along with the carrots and celery.
  • The venison filling can be made up to 2 days in advance and stored in the refrigerator, making pie assembly quicker on St. Andrew's Day.
  • Serve these hearty pies with creamy mashed potatoes, roasted root vegetables, or steamed greens for a complete and satisfying Scottish meal.
